title: Jesus, Whose Blood So Freely Streamed
description: Jesus, Whose Blood So Freely Streamed in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 22, “Jehovam-Shalem, The Lord send peace. Judg 6:24”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, whose blood so free-ly streamed To sa-tis-fy the laws de-mand; By thee from guilt and wrath re-deemed, Be-fore the Fa-ther's face I stand.

lines: Jesus, whose blood so freely streamed
To satisfy the laws demand;
By thee from guilt and wrath redeemed,
Before the Father's face I stand.
To reconcile offending man,
Make Justice drop her angry rod;
What creature could have formed the plan,
Or who fulfil it but a God?
No drop remains of all the curse;
For wretches who deserved the whole;
No arrows dipped in wrath to pierce
The guilty, but returning soul.
Peace by such means co dearly bought,
What rebel could have hoped to see?
Peace, by his injured sovereign wrought,
His Sovereign fastened to the tree.
Now, Lord, thy feeble worm prepare!
For strife with earth and hell begins;
Confirm and gird me for the war,
They hate the soul that hates his sins.
Let them in horrid league agree!
They may assault, they may distress;
But cannot quench thy love to me,
Nor rob me of the Lord my peace.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
